chunks.heading: PR-101 — Customer onboarding
chunks.text:
> **Demonstration document.** This is an internal procedure written for a demonstration.
> It is not a real bank's procedure and carries no authority of its own. Where it states a
> legal requirement it cites the section it comes from, and those citations are real: they
> were retrieved from the Code of Federal Regulations on 17 August 2026 and can be checked.
> Everything else — the internal deadlines, the escalation paths, the naming — is invented.

chunks.heading: PR-101 — Customer onboarding > Purpose
chunks.text:
This procedure covers the checks performed before a customer relationship is opened, and
the point at which a file must go to Compliance rather than be decided by the relationship
team.

chunks.heading: PR-101 — Customer onboarding > Identifying a legal entity customer
chunks.text:
For a legal entity customer, two things must be identified before the account is opened.

**The owners.** Each individual who owns 25 percent or more of the equity interests must
be identified — `31 CFR 1010.230(d)(1)`. Where the chain runs through intermediate
holdings, it is followed until the individuals at the end of it are known.

**The control person.** In addition to any owners, a single individual with significant
responsibility to control, manage or direct the entity must be identified —
`31 CFR 1010.230(d)(2)`. This is one individual, not all of them: a chief executive or an
equivalent senior manager satisfies it.

Both are performed **at the time a new account is opened**, not afterwards —
`31 CFR 1010.230(a)`.

Certain customers are excluded from the beneficial ownership requirement, among them banks
regulated by a Federal functional regulator, registered investment companies and
SEC-registered issuers.

chunks.heading: PR-101 — Customer onboarding > Documents
chunks.text:
The file is complete before any decision is taken. A document that cannot be read is
treated as not provided, and an expired identity document is not acceptable. The name
carried by the document must match the name declared on the application; where it does
not, the difference is documented before the file proceeds.

These are internal controls. They are not imposed by a single section of the regulation,
and this procedure does not pretend otherwise.

chunks.heading: PR-101 — Customer onboarding > Internal deadlines
chunks.text:
*Invented for this demonstration.*

Analysis is completed within five working days of the file being complete. Under enhanced
due diligence this becomes ten working days, to allow the Compliance review. An incomplete
file is notified to the relationship manager within 48 hours; with no response after
thirty days the request is closed and must be started again.

chunks.heading: PR-101 — Customer onboarding > When a file goes to Compliance
chunks.text:
- an owner above the 25 percent threshold cannot be identified
- the control person cannot be identified
- residence or declared operations touch a high-risk jurisdiction
- the declared volume bears no relation to the stated activity
- any screening result requires review before the relationship opens

chunks.heading: PR-101 — Customer onboarding > Retention
chunks.text:
*Invented for this demonstration.* Onboarding records are retained for five years after
the relationship closes. Note that the retention period for a filed suspicious activity
report is set by regulation and is different — see PR-301.

chunks.heading: PR-201 — Transaction monitoring
chunks.text:
> **Demonstration document.** Internal procedure written for a demonstration. The two
> reporting thresholds it refers to are real and cited; the alert handling around them is
> invented.

chunks.heading: PR-201 — Transaction monitoring > Currency transactions
chunks.text:
A currency transaction of **more than $10,000** is reported by the institution —
`31 CFR 1010.311`. This is a reporting obligation on the amount alone. It is not a
suspicion, it carries no judgement about the customer, and it is separate from the
suspicious activity report covered in PR-301.

The two are frequently confused, and the confusion runs one way: staff assume that having
filed a currency report discharges the suspicion obligation. It does not. Where the same
transaction is both above the currency threshold and suspicious, both are filed.

chunks.heading: PR-201 — Transaction monitoring > Alert handling
chunks.text:
*Invented for this demonstration.*

An alert is worked within fifteen working days of being raised. The clock runs from the
alert, not from the analyst picking it up.

Each alert is closed in one of three ways: no further action with the reason recorded,
a request for information from the relationship manager, or escalation to Compliance.
An alert closed without a recorded reason is treated as not closed.

chunks.heading: PR-201 — Transaction monitoring > Typologies
chunks.text:
*Invented for this demonstration.* The categories used to classify an alert:

**Structuring** — amounts arranged to sit below a reporting threshold, split across days,
branches or instruments.

**Rapid movement** — funds credited and moved out with no economic purpose stated, leaving
the account at or near nil.

**Sanctions nexus** — a name, a bank or an owner in the chain relates to a designated
person or a restricted jurisdiction.

**Unusual counterparty** — a counterparty unrelated to the declared business, or newly
incorporated with no trading history.

**Cash intensity** — a proportion of cash inconsistent with the sector or with the
customer's own declared activity.

chunks.heading: PR-201 — Transaction monitoring > What monitoring cannot do
chunks.text:
*Invented for this demonstration, and worth stating plainly.*

A monitoring system produces alerts, not conclusions. The proportion of alerts that lead
to a report is small, and lowering the detection threshold does not raise that proportion
— it raises the volume of work while the number of genuine cases stays roughly where it
was. Any change to a threshold is accompanied by an estimate of the analyst hours it
creates, because a threshold nobody can staff is a threshold that quietly stops being
applied.

chunks.heading: PR-301 — Suspicious activity reporting
chunks.text:
> **Demonstration document.** Internal procedure written for a demonstration. Where it
> states a legal requirement it cites the section, and those citations are real —
> retrieved from the Code of Federal Regulations on 17 August 2026. The internal steps
> around them are invented.

chunks.heading: PR-301 — Suspicious activity reporting > What triggers a report
chunks.text:
A transaction is reportable when it is conducted or attempted by, at or through the bank
and **it involves or aggregates at least $5,000** — `31 CFR 1020.320(a)(2)`.

The threshold is on the amount, not on the certainty. A report is made where there is a
suspicion; it does not require proof, and it does not require the underlying offence to
have been identified or named. An analysis concluding that an explanation *cannot be
ruled out* is a basis for reporting.

chunks.heading: PR-301 — Suspicious activity reporting > Deadline
chunks.text:
The report is filed **no later than 30 calendar days after the date of initial detection**
of the facts that may constitute a basis for filing — `31 CFR 1020.320(b)(3)`.

Where no suspect has been identified on the date of detection, filing may be delayed a
further 30 calendar days to identify one. **In no case is reporting delayed more than 60
calendar days** after initial detection.

"Initial detection" is the date the facts became known, not the date the review concluded.
A review that takes three weeks does not extend the deadline; it consumes it.

chunks.heading: PR-301 — Suspicious activity reporting > Confidentiality
chunks.text:
**No bank, and no director, officer, employee or agent of any bank, shall disclose a
report or any information that would reveal the existence of one** —
`31 CFR 1020.320(e)`.

The prohibition is absolute and it is not limited to speech. It applies to systems as much
as to people: no commercially accessible tool may allow the existence of a report to be
inferred, including by an indirect signal such as an unexplained block, a status that
appears nowhere else, or a queue only certain staff can see.

*Invented for this demonstration:* where a customer asks directly, the relationship manager
neither confirms nor denies, and refers the question to Compliance without recording the
exchange in the commercial file.

chunks.heading: PR-301 — Suspicious activity reporting > Filing before execution
chunks.text:
*Invented for this demonstration.* Where the operation has not yet been executed, the
report is made before execution, unless that is materially impossible or unless the delay
would risk alerting the customer.

chunks.heading: PR-301 — Suspicious activity reporting > Retention
chunks.text:
**A copy of the report and the original or business record equivalent of any supporting
documentation is retained for five years from the date of filing** —
`31 CFR 1020.320(d)`.

Supporting documentation means what the analysis actually relied on: the transaction
records, the screening results, the notes of the review. It is held on restricted access,
and *(invented)* the list of people holding that access is reviewed each half-year.

chunks.heading: PR-401 — Screening and customer exposure
chunks.text:
> **Demonstration document.** Internal procedure written for a demonstration. Almost
> everything below is invented: the United States does not impose a single threshold for
> screening or a fixed treatment of politically exposed persons in the way this procedure
> describes. Where a real requirement is cited, it is marked as such and can be checked.

chunks.heading: PR-401 — Screening and customer exposure > Screening at onboarding
chunks.text:
*Invented for this demonstration.* Names are screened before the relationship opens, and
again whenever an owner or control person changes. The screening covers the customer, the
individuals identified under `31 CFR 1010.230(d)(1)` and `(d)(2)`, and the declared
counterparties.

chunks.heading: PR-401 — Screening and customer exposure > Match strength
chunks.text:
*Invented for this demonstration, and the operational heart of this procedure.*

A screening result is not a yes or a no. A common name returns dozens of near-matches, and
the work is in the middle of the range rather than at either end.

- a strong match is reviewed by Compliance before the relationship opens
- a weak or partial match is documented and reviewed by the analyst
- a match that is ambiguous — the same date of birth with a different middle name, a
  transliteration that could go either way — goes to Compliance, because an analyst
  clearing it alone leaves nothing to defend later

The last case is the expensive one and the one worth staffing for. It is neither a hit nor
a miss; it is a judgement, and judgements are the part that must be written down.

chunks.heading: PR-401 — Screening and customer exposure > Politically exposed persons
chunks.text:
*Invented for this demonstration.* Holding public office is not in itself a ground for
refusal, and this procedure does not treat it as one. It raises the level of review: the
source of wealth is documented, and the file is approved by Compliance rather than by the
relationship team.

chunks.heading: PR-401 — Screening and customer exposure > Restricted jurisdictions
chunks.text:
*Invented for this demonstration.* Residence in, or declared operations into, a
jurisdiction under sectoral restriction sends the file to Compliance regardless of amount.
Volume matters for the monitored jurisdictions, not for the restricted ones.

chunks.heading: PR-401 — Screening and customer exposure > What screening does not establish
chunks.text:
A match is not a finding. It is a reason to look. Where looking produces a suspicion, the
obligation that follows is the one in PR-301 — filed within 30 calendar days of initial
detection, `31 CFR 1020.320(b)(3)` — and the fact that a screening result started it
changes neither the deadline nor the confidentiality that attaches to it.
